title: Rotokakahi A3B1B1B — list of owners as at 14 Aug 1940 (Matiu Wiripo and three Rihari Matiu children) with schedule of ownership orders 1969–1990
summary: Nine pages (area 57:3:36 = 23.4363 ha; 63.636 shares). The 1940 list has just four owners: MATIU WIRIPO 36.363 (4/7) and Rirena Arama @ Rirena Rihari Matiu, "Tame Rihari Matiu @ Manuera Rihari Matiu" and Whina Rihari Matiu, 9.091 each (1/7) — the block came down through Matiu Wiripo, with Rihari Matiu's three children already holding their father's share. Then: (a) 4 Nov 1969 Rirena vested her 9.091 in her sons Makura (4.546) and Charlie Arama (4.545); (b) 3 Mar 1970 Matiu Wiripo's 36.363 was divided among his lines (S.V.O., KT 6/32-13): Wiremu Matiu and Reta Waipouri (2.577 each), the seven "Te Okena Matiu" children (Topia, Takuira, Pataraki or Pataraki Atama, Manuera, Iwa, Mane…), Te Okena and Hone Piriparaihe (Ruhia's line), the four Rihari Matiu children Rirena, Rata, Hira and HARE (1.299 each), the Maihi/Rurawhe line, the Wikitaringi Taitimu line, the Hapakuku, Wharewaka and Wi Hone lines; (c) 9 Nov 1970 WHINA's 9.091 went solely to "Rirena Rihari Matiu or Rirena Arama of Pawarenga" (KT 6/315); (d) 20 Oct 1981 Rirena's 10.390 to her EIGHT children — Lucy Nicholas, Michael, Makura, Graham, Andrew, Ken Arama, Hannah Wano and Charlie Arama, 1.299 each; (e) 1990 Makura's share to Michael Arama and Charlie's to Hannah Wano. Also Arapeta Peri Paraihe (list 15, 1.731) to the Public Trustee, 1982. The 1970 succession is the Court's own statement that the Te Okena (Atama) Matiu children, Ruhia's Piriparaihe sons and Rihari Matiu's children were all Matiu Wiripo's descendants.

title: Rotokakahi A — succession register 1889–1896: Wiremu Paraihe and Mereana Paraihe to Peri Paraihe, Hira Amuketi and Mereana Pirini (16 Mar 1896)
summary: Four register pages for the parent block Rotokakahi A, successions 1889–1896. Page 3 carries the earliest Paraihe record in this collection: WIREMU PARAIHE (d. 19 Dec 1891) and MEREANA PARAIHE, each succeeded on 16 March 1896 by Peri Paraihe (m), Hira Amuketi (f) and Mereana Pirini (f), one third each — the same three who took Hone Paraihe's Whakakoro F4 interest in 1914 (Hira by then dead and represented by her Amuketi children). This confirms Hira Amuketi as Peri Paraihe's sister and adds two more Paraihe (Wiremu and Mereana) who died before 1896 and whose relationship — sibling or parent — the register does not state. Also the Tipene (Hone Tana Papahia), Rikihana, Paraone, Hokopu and other families of Rotokakahi A.

title: Rotokakahi A3B1B1B — succession order schedule: Peri Paraihe (1936), Ria Hone Wharewaka (1940) and the exchange orders of 14 Aug 1940 consolidating Peri Paraihe's interest in Rirena, Tame and Whina Rihari Matiu
summary: Form 16 schedule for Rotokakahi A3B1B1B. (1) Peri Paraihe alias Kaperiere Paraihe (d. 1929): the same nine-way succession of 25 Sep 1936 as in Whakakoro F4 and Oturu A, with Rirena Arama trustee for Whina and Ria Hone Wharewaka trustee for the Okena Peri children. (2) Ria Hone Wharewaka (d. by 1940): her fifth to Wati Ratahi Topia, Erina, Rauriti, Ani and Ihaka Hone Wharewaka. (3) Two EXCHANGE ORDERS of 14 Aug 1940 (HK 17/294-5 and 296-7) by which Arapeta and Hone Peri Paraihe, the three Okena Peri children and Ria's five successors all gave up their Rotokakahi A3B1B1B shares to Rirena, Tame (Manuera) and Whina Rihari Matiu — so that by the 14 Aug 1940 list (doc 1279339) Rihari Matiu's three children held the whole of Peri Paraihe's 3/7 of the block (9.091 each) beside Matiu Wiripo's 4/7. This is the mechanism by which the Rihari Matiu line consolidated Peri Paraihe's Rotokakahi interest — and, presumably, gave up shares elsewhere in return.

summary: Register page (MLC 16A schedule) for Rotokakahi A No 3, successions 1896–1906, ending with the Hira Amuketi succession of 4 Oct 1906. title: Auckland minute book 11 AT 300 — sitting of 17 November 1980: Rirena Arama (s 78A) — Erihapeti Arama 'also known as Betty' sworn as applicant and daughter; nine children listed; will not produced (item 60, continues on 301)
blocks_recorded: (minute book page — Rirena Arama's estate; her interests were in Rotokakahi A3B1B1B, Paihia 1D1E2, Owhata C and the Peri Paraihe blocks)
court: Māori Land Court, Tai Tokerau (sitting at Auckland)
summary: One handwritten page, folio 300 of Auckland minute book 11 (book scan 01076422), margin date 17.11.80. (a) Tail of an earlier, unrelated item: '… and transfer to person entitled. Please return probate to Mrs Thorne(?) with form. Fee on application is remitted and to be applied to Registrar's application for vesting.' (b) Item 60: 'RIRENA ARAMA (S. 78A). Erihapeti Arama: Applicant. Sworn: Also known as Betty. My mother died on the 26th April 1980 at Pa[wa]renga. I was present at her tangi. She left a will. Court: Who are present in Court. Present: 1. Lucy Nicholas f.a. [Māngere]; 2. Betty or Erihapeti Hori f.a. [c/- Mauku, R.D. 3 Pukekohe]; 3. [a first name struck through, "Michael" written above] Michael Arama m.a. c/- No 1 above; 4. Makura Arama m.a. [Manurewa]; 5. Graham Arama m.a. [Māngere]; 6. Andrew Arama m.a. c/- No 4; 7. Ken Arama m.a. [Papakura]; 8. Hannah Wano f.a. c/- P.O. Ōpononi [margin: Absent]; 9. Charlie Arama m.a. c/- No 1. Court: The will has not been produced, only an unsigned copy. The solicitor has will. Registrar to write and ask for its production. Family are to discuss with Mr Noa[—]' — the sentence runs on to folio 301. Street addresses are in the minute but are not reproduced here. Significance: Betty/Erihapeti Hori swears that Rirena was her mother, and the Court lists her as one of nine children present or accounted for — the same sibling set that took Rirena's Paihia, Rotokakahi and Owhata interests on 20 Oct 1981 (AT 12/360), minus Betty. The will was still outstanding on 1 Jul 1981 (12 AT 232, item 62: solicitor Malcolm Douglas, Manurewa).

title: Auckland minute book 11 AT 353 — sitting of 20 November 1980: Rirena Arama (s 78A, item 60 continued) — 'the titles officer has discussed an arrangement with the family'; provisional orders offered pending the original will
blocks_recorded: (minute book page — Rirena Arama's estate, continued from folios 300/301; her interests were in Rotokakahi A3B1B1B, Owhata C, Te Puna o Hokianga and the Paihia 1D1 blocks)
court: Māori Land Court, Tai Tokerau (sitting at Auckland)
summary: One handwritten page, folio 353 of Auckland minute book 11 (book scan 01076422), margin date 20.11.80. (a) The upper two-thirds belong to another family's matter: 'Order: s 136 as follows — Panguru B30 5, value $245, to Nos 1–4 above 1/9th share each, No 11 1/9th solely, Nos 12–18 1/63rd, Nos 19–21 1/27th, Nos 24–28 1/45th, Nos 32–34 and 37–42 1/81st. The above block has potential afforestation value. Wharau 5 to Adelaide Wood(?), No … above, solely. Rebecca's children were present when all agreed that only one person be put in to this small interest and that as the youngest surviving daughter it should go to Adelaide.' A later note in another hand — '(Refer to AT 16/219-220 for final [orders])' — sits between the two items and most probably belongs to that matter. (b) '60 (cont'd) RIRENA ARAMA, S. 78A. See folio 300/301. Court: The titles officer has discussed an arrangement with the family. The Court awaits production of original will but is prepared to make provisional orders subject to ratification by Judge in Chambers when original will to hand.' The page ends there; the provisional orders themselves should follow on folio 354. Read with 11 AT 300 (17 Nov 1980: Erihapeti/Betty applicant, nine children listed), 12 AT 232 (1 Jul 1981: will still outstanding; Wiremu Arama's interests vested in Betty alone) and the final order AT 12/360 (20 Oct 1981, 'in terms of will', to the other eight), this is the Court's own record that the 1981 outcome was a negotiated family arrangement.

title: Order vesting the interests of Rirena Arama or Arana or Rirena Rihari Matiu, deceased, in her successors in terms of her will — Whangārei, 20 Oct 1981, Judge A. G. McHugh (AT 12/360; s 78A Maori Affairs Amendment Act 1967; 2 pages)
court: Māori Land Court, Tokerau District (sitting at Whangārei)
summary: Form M.L.C. 88 'Order Vesting Interest of Deceased in Successors' (Maori Affairs Amendment Act 1967, s 78A — the 1953 Act heading struck), Tokerau District, sitting at Whangārei on 20 October 1981 before Ashley George McHugh Esq., Judge, in the matter of an application to succeed to RIRENA ARAMA or ARANA or RIRENA RIHARI MATIU, deceased: her interests in the scheduled lands vested in the persons shown as from the 26th day of April 1980; sealed, signed by the Deputy Registrar. SCHEDULE — 'IN TERMS OF WILL': Rotokakahi A3B1B1B (value $680), Owhata C ($376) and Te Puna o Hokianga ($34) to 1 Lucy Nicholas f.a., 2 Michael Arama m.a., 3 Makura Arama m.a., 4 Graham Arama m.a., 5 Andrew Arama m.a., 6 Ken Arama m.a., 7 Hannah Wano f.a., 8 Charlie Arama m.a. — EQUALLY (entered/checked stamps 1982; a word in the share column against no. 7, possibly 'cancelled', is unclear). Erihapeti (Betty) Arama or Hori — the applicant of 17 Nov 1980 and one of the nine children listed then (11 AT 300) — receives nothing under this order, which follows the will. Addresses (Māngere, Manurewa, Papakura, Ōpononi) are on the order but not reproduced here.

title: Paihia 1D1C — succession order schedule 1929–1950 (7 pages): Ruhia Peri Matiu and the Peri Matiu children
summary: Seven pages of Form 16 succession order schedules for Paihia 1D1C. Key whānau entries (p.1, all 3 July 1929, HK 10/94): three children who died young — "Roi Matiu" (1906), "Hoana Peri Matiu" (1907) and "Hana Peri Matiu" (1909) — succeeded by "Ruhia Peri Matiu, f.a." solely (Hana's half shared with Iri Tamaho Maika). This is Ruhia Matiu Wiripo, Peri Paraihe's second wife, recorded under her married form "Ruhia Peri Matiu", with a small annotation of a further name (Horomona / Paura Taitimu). In 1940 she took 1/8 of Parani Ritete alias Parani Rewi (d. 1916) alongside Iri Tamaho Maika (1/8) — an unexplained close tie to the Ritete/Rewi whānau — and her and Iri's interests were the subject of an exchange order (HK 17/315, 16.8.40). Page 5 repeats the Pati Wharewaka succession of 13.8.40 with her full name "Pati Wharewaka Topia" and Atama Matiu as trustee. Other Paihia 1D1C families: Ritete/Pirini/Tahana, Ihaka Uruhau, Hira Tukino, Herehana, Taitimu Tahana, Angel, Karaweia/Rameka/Matiu Kapa.

summary: Three pages of the Waihapa succession register (two handwritten register pages and a Form 16 schedule). Page 2: HARE HONGI HIKA, succession order 27 February 1890 (N4/119) to Rongo Kahira (m), Mereana Paora (f), TURA WIREMU (f), Rati Pona (m), Wini Tuta (m), Huia Miriama (f), Arihia Hemi (f) and Poni Rewharewha (f). This is the clearest Court record of Tura — "Tura Hongi" on the 1876 memorial, "Tura Wiremu" here after her marriage to Wiremu Tangata — succeeding to her father, and it fixes the membership of the Hāre Hongi Hika descent group that reappears as group A in the 1895 Pokaka title. Other entries: Ruinga Tapu (1880), Te Arama / Hone Kingi Tapu (1885), Hori Kerei, the Toetoe family (1890), Aporo te Meawai, Wakahe alias Te Hie, Meta Tapu, Erana Raupane alias Erana Ururoa (to the Snowden children, 1894), Mio Tuauru (1910).

title: Taupo 23C — succession order schedule: Taniora Rihari or Rihari Taniora (d. 1922), order 29 Feb 1932; Matire Taniora (d. 1918); Manga Taniora Rihari (1962)
summary: Two-page Form 16 succession order schedule for Taupo 23C. Page 2 is the key whānau record: "Taniora Rihari or Rihari Taniora", died 1922 (N66A/99), succession order 29 February 1932 dividing his interest into SEVENTHS — (1) Manga Taniora Rihari m, (2) Rihari Taniora Rihari m, (3) the seven children of the late Hetaraka Taniora at 1/49 each (Maki, Hoana, Pera, Te Hape or Hone, Te Kui or Marara, Himi, Pueti; trustee Rahera Hetaraka Taniora), (4) the EIGHT children of the late Arama Taniora at 1/56 each — Mane, Peepi, WIREMU, Arama or Honetiaki II, Raiha, Taitimu, Mio and Rirena Arama Taniora — with "Tr: PETI WIREMU TANGATA" (their mother Erihapeti, Arama Taniora's widow), (5) Werahiko and Te Uinga Pereene Kini, Maori Moana Tarapatiki and Peka Toma Ngarangi at 1/28, (6) Mita and Tupakongia Heremaia Kingi at 1/14 (trustee Peti Kingi), (7) the four Hamuera Herewini children at 1/28 — who also took, 1/4 each, the interest of Matire Taniora (d. 1918, N66A/102), evidently their mother and Taniora Rihari's daughter. Years written beside the minors (1924–1943) are coming-of-age years. A 1962 succession vesting order (N 86/126) passes Manga Taniora Rihari's share solely to Maria Maudy Rihari. Page 1: Maata Putete Hape (d. 1933) to eight Hare Paora/Hongi successors (1938); Matarae Arano (d. 31.12.32) to Mere Matarae Arano (1951). This one page gives Taniora Rihari's seven lines of descent and names all eight of Arama Taniora and Peti's children — including a second "Rirena" (Rirena Arama Taniora, b. c. 1912, Wiremu Arama's sister), distinct from Rirena Theresa Arama née Rihari Matiu (b. c. 1911), Wiremu's wife.

title: Taupo 23C — compiled list of owners as at 28 Aug 1957 (38 owners, 36.000 shares) with schedule of ownership orders 1932–1957
summary: Four pages: (1) typed "Compiled List of Owners as at 28/8/57" for Taupo 23C (38:0:20; 36.000 shares), 38 owners; (2–4) the typed schedule of ownership orders, entries 9–56. The original owners (list nos 1–8) included ARAMA TANIORA (no. 1, 5.000 shares — N66A/100), "HIMI TANIORA RIHARI" (no. 2, 4.000 — N66A/99, i.e. Taniora Rihari under a third recorded name), Matarae Arano (5, 5.000), Matire Taniora (6, 4.000), Maata Putete Hape (7, 6.000) and Rihari Taniora Rihari (8, 4.000). Rihari Taniora Rihari: 4.000 + 0.571 = 4.571 (as in 2009).

title: Auckland minute book 12 AT 232 — sitting of 1 July 1981: Rirena Rihari Matiu (Mrs Arama), succession held up pending her will (item 62); Wiremu Arama Taniora dec'd, Erihapeti Arama sworn as applicant and daughter (item 72, continues on 233)
blocks_recorded: (minute book page — Wiremu Arama Taniora and Rirena Rihari Matiu successions; the 1 Jul 1981 order covered Taupo 23C, Tauaki, Mangaiti 3B, Waihapa 2B4B and Otangaroa 1C3B1)
court: Māori Land Court, Tai Tokerau (sitting at Auckland)
summary: One handwritten page, folio 232 of Auckland minute book 12 (Pātaka Whenua page 233 of book scan 01076095), headed 'Auckland … 1.7.81'. Three items. (a) Tail of an earlier application about a lease fixture: 'with the consent of the lessee, the Maori Land Board, the Commissioner of Crown Lands. Court: Discussed matter with parties. The application is adjourned to a fixture to be arranged by the applicant or his solicitor after consultation with the Board, Mr [Moanan?] or his solicitor and the Court Registrar. Adjourned in interim to next Whangarei [sitting] but may be later adjourned if negotiations still proceeding.' Copies to the Maori Land Board, Mr [Moanan?] and Mr [Rahiti?] of [Pegg Bros?] — not whānau business. (b) Item 62, '3 copies 1.7.81': 'RIRENA RIHARI MATIU (Mrs ARAMA) (S 78A/67). Court: I refer to AT 11/300-301. Acting Registrar is to write to Malcolm Douglas, Solicitor, Manurewa and request him to forward original will to Court so that succession can be completed. File to be referred to Court for order when will received.' — i.e. Rirena (T901, d. 1980) left a will held by a Manurewa solicitor, and her succession (made 20 Oct 1981, AT 12/360) waited on it. (c) Item 72, '3 copies 1.7.81': 'WIREMU ARAMA TANIORA Dec'd (S 135). Erihapeti Arama sworn: I am the applicant. The deceased was my father. Died at Pawarenga on the 4th June 1966. I was' — the evidence continues on folio 233 (not in this file). This is the minute behind the 1 Jul 1981 sole succession of 'Betty or Erihapeti Arama or Hori' to Wiremu Arama's interests (order 136/53) in Taupo 23C, Tauaki, Mangaiti 3B, Waihapa 2B4B and Otangaroa 1C3B1.

title: Minute book 15 HK 261 — succession to Peri Paraihe alias Kaperiere Paraihe, whakapapa read in Court (25 Sep 1936)
court: Native Land Court, Tokerau District, sitting at Pawarenga
summary: Hokianga minute book 15, folio 261, 25 September 1936. Applications 246–258 (plus Paihia 1M3A and Wairoa A) — succession to Peri Paraihe alias Kaperiere Paraihe in fifteen blocks. The Court read out the whakapapa supplied by Mr Tamaho McMath: 1st wife Horomena Toriwhina = Peri Paraihe = 2nd wife Ruhia Matiu Wiripo. By the 1st wife: Maraea (deceased) = Rihari Matiu, whose children are Rirena Arama (f.a.), Tame Rihari Matiu (m.a.) and Whina Rihari Matiu (f., 18); and Ria Hone Wharewaka (f.a.). By the 2nd wife: Hone Peri Paraihe (m.a.); Okena P.P. (deceased), whose children are Rawiri Okena Peri (m., 15), Ngarimu (f., 9) and Hone (m., 13); Pirini P.P. (deceased, no issue); Arapeta P.P. (m.a.). Written approval of the whakapapa and request that all share in proper proportion lodged by Ria, Hone, Arapeta, Rirena and Tame; all present except Hone (ill). A will dated 5/8/27 lodged by Tamaho McMath at Rawene 9/9/36 was far too late for probate and the Court would not have approved its contents; the family agreed it be taken no notice of. Deceased died 7 September 1929. Orders: succession orders accordingly in favour of all nine as above; trustee for Whina to be [name illegible]; trustee for Okena's children to be Ria.

title: Te Kohanga No. 1 — original list of owners (1867), succession schedules 1875–1962, schedule of ownership orders, and compiled list as at 6 Mar 1963 (171 owners, 25.000 shares; 41a 2r 0p)
summary: Forty-six pages (hand-written MLC 102 / Form 16 schedules, then typed): (1) F. E. Maning's 1867 list of the 25 persons interested in Te Kohanga No. 1 under s.17 of the Native Lands Act 1867 — Mumu Ngapipi, Puhipi, Te Pana, Hamihana, Kingi Wiremu, Nepia, Honi Te Karaparapa, Timoti Puhipi, Te Waaka Rangaunu, Taipari (the ten named in the Crown grant), Poharama, Te Henare, Paora, Te Kirihini Nepia, Te Rapihana, Ranga, Takerei, Hamiora, Patana, Meri, Erina, Herepete, Wiremu Tana Hamihana, Hapita, Makoare Haki; (2) succession orders 1875–1909 (Kingi Wiremu, Te Pana, Takerei, Erina, the 1896 sitting — Meri → Raniera Matiu and Tamihana Rihimona; Makoare Haki; Herepete; Hamihana Paka; **Hamiora Rungaiterangi alias Hamiora → Rihipeti Arama, Hariata Haimona, Te Wikiriwhi Poutu, 5.9.1896** — Te Waaka Rangaunu, Honi te Karaparapa, Nepia, Patana te Maru (1901), Poharama Karanui (1905), Mumu Ngapipi and Taipari (1909)); (3) orders 1912–62 including Rihipeti Arama (d. 17.12.1922) → Eruera Paora (1925) → the Eruera Wahapu / Makinira Wiremu children (1944), the big Whangaroa/Kaitaia sitting of 18–19 Nov 1931 (N66A), Kiritiana Matiu → her Matiu children (1936, as on Karikari 2), the Hohipa, Mihaka, Nopera Arano and Natanahira lines and the 1949 exchange orders against Parengarenga 5B2B; (4) the typed schedule of ownership orders (nos 26–338); (5) the compiled list of 171 owners as at 6.3.1963 (25.000 shares). The 1965 Te Kohanga (Lots 1, 3–27) list of 329 owners / 1,745 shares (docs 1391494, 1391616) is a later, larger title.

title: Takou Block — ownership schedule under the amalgamation order of 4 May 1991 (323.9320 ha; 665,000 shares): 420 owners, with the schedule of ownership orders nos 421–516, July 1991 – June 1998 (22 pages)
summary: Pages 1–10: the typed owners list attached to the Takou Block amalgamation order of 04/05/91 (LAND Takou Block; AREA 323.9320 ha; TOTAL SHARE 665000.000), 420 owners in alphabetical order of first name with sex/age and relative interest, hand-annotated with strike-throughs and the numbers of the later entries that replaced them; file no. 14236. Pages 11–22: the handwritten M.A. 835 'Schedule of ownership orders', entries 421–516 (10 Jul 1991 – 15 Jun 1998) — successions, vestings, gifts and whānau-trust orders citing Whangarei (WH), Kaikohe (KH), Aotea (AT), Rotorua, Ōtorohanga and Whakatāne minute books. Largest interests: Horitina Hori Tareha 24,623; Te Hira Mou Wiremu 22,150; Wi Parihi Mou Wiremu 21,716; Aperere Watene / Alfred Williams 18,937; Himi (Kutu) Hone Puru 17,771; Haare Puru 17,769; Ronald Taylor Hou 17,346; Edna Mary Paul 14,518 (life); Ngapine Reihana 12,901; Ngapine Haki 12,590; Hokena Wi Haare 12,027. Family groups visible from equal interests: Rihari (Hamuhamu Te Kiri, Ramiri, Tokowha, Whaekaimau 1,480.618 each; Sophie Robina, Taku, Ture, Whakaropai 357.449 each; Te Atarangi 2,323.558; Hetana 2,410.947; Meeke 1,479.791; Rehi 531.281), Kanuta Paerau, Kaiawe Parangi, Heihei, Kira, Haare, Hikuwai, Moana Hira, Rameka, Tahere, Tuhi, Tihi, Napia (388.122 each), Henry, Moihi. Whānau-relevant names: Mihiarangi Hulena or Taniora (2,741.935) and Warren Taniora (3,789.575 — the same figure as Rebecca Schneider); the Henry family (Maryanne 1,384.435 = Tania Dorretta Poulson; Teresa 2,675.389; Micheal John, Paul Stuart, Steven Richard, Wayne Andrew c. 374–378) — cf. Hoana Hetaraka Taniora 'or Hoana Henry' (T097); Ngawai Amato Riwhi Moihi 914.435 and Reupena Huperio Riwhi Moihi 4,595.820 — the Moihi/Amato whānau also on Tauaki (Arama Moihi alias Amato Riwhi Moihi, d. before 1917) and Taupo (Huperio Moihi, 1913; Taiapo Arama and Hapeta Arama Amato, Taupo No. 11); Paora Pita Taiapo and Manawhakaora Taiapo (Paora) — cf. the Taiapo Pita / Wirihana Taiapo owners of Te Wainui 2G; the Napia family (cf. Hare Napia, Otangaroa 1875); Taku Rihari and Aperahama Kaiawe Parangi, also owners of Waimate North; and the Kira, Wati Haare, Tame Hikuwai, Heihei and Taumaunu owners shared with Wainui A (1958) and Matauri X (1970). Arithmetic note: the 420 typed interests as read sum to 662,000.000 against the stated 665,000.000; the 3,000-share gap has not been located (either one thousands digit misread, or a typing error in the schedule).

title: Matangirau — hand-written list of owners by family group, with hapū (c. 1890s–1900s; ~90 names, part of a longer list numbered to 93)
summary: Three hand-written pages (no form): page 1 headed "Hiria Pa Matangirau …" lists owners with ages and a hapū column — the Tangiwai, Wirihana, Tame Te Awa, Rewi Paapu, Puatau, Haki Waata, Manahara Pona and Taniwha families; pages 2–3 (numbered 45–93) give the Paoro Hori, Nako Tauranga, Wiremu Ihaia, Hare Wiremu Ihaia, Honetua, Keepa, Himiona Maaka, Paerata and Taniwha families. The same Whangaroa whānau appear on the Wainui and Matauri records (Wiremu Ihaia, Kepa Tupe, Manahara, Himiona Maaka).

summary: One typed Form 16 schedule of successors for the Te Wainui block, 1890–1901: Te Kingi Kira (1892 → Kingi Hori, Huhana Kingi); Pataromu Tangaroa (1890 → Haare Neke, Matiu Pataromu, Wi Haare); Tipene Manu (→ Ihimaera Pawa, Reta Waitohi, Tamati Pera); Kingi Hori Kingi alias Kingi Hori (→ Awha, Pikake, Wharemarama, Puti Kingi Hori and Huhana Manahara, trustee); Te Kepa Tupe alias Henare te Kepa Tupe (1894 → seven Kepa Tupe children, trustee Heni Tupe); Huhana Kingi alias Huhana Manahara (→ Taniwha, Ngatau, Mangu, Taipari Manahara); Hone Ritotahi (→ Akinihi Mita, Mate Nako); Tame Kamohoro (1901 → Tira Haare); Hohepa Whare (1901 → Hone Taotahi, Mereana Hawira, Raina Pakia); Parao Nohorai (→ Eme Patuhu); Waitohi (1901 → Tamati Pera 1/2 and the Manahara and Kingi Hori children 1/16 each). These are the ancestors of the 1958 Wainui A–C owners.

title: Tutukau East Z — 1957 title (P.O. 30 May 1957): schedule of 675 original owners, annotated to 11 Apr 1963 (755 owners), with succession-order schedules 1959–62 and ownership-order schedules 1983–87 (137 pages)
summary: Header (p.1): BLOCK Tutukau East Z; LIST TO 11.4.63; OWNERS BEFORE 755; ORIGINAL OWNERS 675; TITLE P.O. 30.5.1957; AREA 4716a 3r 20p; PLAN nil. Pages 1–57 are the typed M.L.C. 118A schedule of the 1957 partition order (alphabetical, with sex/age and relative interest), hand-annotated with succession orders made before 1963 (e.g. 'S/O 25-3-60'). Page 34 (schedule p.11), entry 132: 'HORI HORI, m.a., 18.05035' — no annotation, so he had not been succeeded by the 1963 cut-off. Pages 58–65 are the handwritten 'Succession order schedule' for 1959–62 (Rot 115/393–394, Tpo 36/365–366, Taupo 36/4, Ikaroa Na 93/402 etc.); pages 66–137 are M.A. 835 'Schedule of ownership orders' sheets for 1983–87 (list nos. 1192–1405). The 1963–1982 orders — including the succession to Hori Hori — are NOT in this file. Share pattern worth noting: Hori Hori 18.05035, Mapuna te Ngaru 18.05034 and Mary/Sam Rota 18.05033 look like equal portions of one earlier interest, and Hiria te Kiri (or Phillips) already held 3.00840 (one-sixth of 18.05035) in 1957.
